text:
incident-bot: PAGING: Redwood Private - Meridian Health (vpc-72a) reported elevated egress failures to external model endpoints. Severity: P1. Initial detection: 2719994321. Affected: dedicated tenant pool (meridian-dedicated-2), ingress ok, egress failing healthchecks to 3rd-party inference backend. @oncall-sre is paged.

Priya Patel: Seeing the bot. I'm on it. Quick ask: is this only NLB or also ALB paths?

Alex Soto: Meridian's setup: NLB in front of our egress proxies (ephemeral proxies in private subnets) -> NATGW in public subnets for internet egress. Healthchecks from backend are failing on NLB target group. ALB is only for control plane, not in this path.

Nadia K: Confirmed NLB target health = 0/3, instance targets show `tcp/443` failing handshake. Cloud metrics show increased RSTs from targets around 2719994200.

Evan M: I can jump on network side. Checking SG changes and route table updates. No recent terraform apply recorded in last 24h for Meridian.

Customer Support (Meridian): Customers reporting timeouts calling third-party vendor for billing verification. Impact: all webhook-based flows that need external vendor calls are failing. Ticket numbers piling up.

Tony R: Possible causes: conntrack tables on egress proxies filling -> start dropping new outbound flows (results in upstream healthcheck timeouts). Or NATGW ephemeral port exhaustion. Need to check conntrack on the proxies and NAT metrics.

Priya Patel: Running `sudo conntrack -S` on one proxy now, retrieving counters.

Alex Soto: Pulling NATGW metrics (Bytes, Active connections, Port utilization). Also cross-checking NLB logs for connection resets.

incident-bot: Deploy bot notice: No active deploys to meridian-dedicated-2 in the last hour.

Nadia K: Conntrack shows entries skyrocketing, ESTABLISHED ~ 130k on one proxy (conntrack table size = 262144). Eviction spikes at 2719994180. Looks like high short-lived flows.

Evan M: NATGW ephemeral port usage at ~91%. That aligns. When ports exhausted new flows get RST or fail to establish causing NLB healthchecks to appear as failed because backend can't complete.

Priya Patel: Quick mitigation options: 1) Add an additional NATGW in another AZ and shift route table to include it (fast failover), 2) Spin up temporary egress proxy autoscale group with NAT association, 3) Tweak conntrack params to increase max, 4) Adjust NLB healthcheck to be tolerant (short-term). We need to weigh risk/regulatory constraints for Meridian (no public bastion / must avoid open wide ACLs).

Tony R: Meridian's contract prohibits modifying source IP behavior. Adding NATGW or extra egress proxy is allowed as long as we don't change packet source semantics. Option 1 or 2 are fine. Option 3 (conntrack increase) is quick but stateful and may require kernel tuning + restart window — risky for production.

Priya Patel: I'll coordinate a two-step plan: short-term (30 min) = provision extra NATGW + update private route table to prefer new NAT (simple route table edit to add second NAT with equal weighting). mid-term (2-6h) = scale egress proxy ASG + tune long-term autoscaling policy, and add prefix-preserving pooling to reduce ephemeral consumption.

Alex Soto: I'll open infra change: create NATGW in az-b and attach to meridian-private-rt. Preparing cloudformation change. ETA ~ 12 minutes to create NATGW and propagate.

incident-bot: Change freeze check: This is an incident hotfix. Exempting change freeze per oncall decision.

Nadia K: While NATGW is provisioning, I recommend temporarily increasing `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` on egress proxies by +50% to avoid immediate evictions. I can apply via `sysctl -w` and monitor. It's non-persistent but buys time.

Priya Patel: Agreed. Nadia, apply on one proxy first and validate. Evan, standby to roll across the fleet if it looks stable.

Nadia K: Running: 
```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=393216
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=86400
```
Applied to proxy-azc-1. Conntrack usage dropped evictions immediately. Monitoring for 2 minutes.

Evan M: Seeing fewer evictions, backend handshake errors dropping in logs. Good sign.

Alex Soto: NATGW created in az-b, allocation done. Executing route table update to add secondary NAT target (no downtime expected).

incident-bot: Alert: route change initiated by Alex Soto at 2719994700. Automated watchers enabled.

Customer Support (Meridian): Streams look better but some retries still happening. Root cause investigation ticket assigned to PrimeOps.

Priya Patel: Monitoring NLB target health. If health returns to healthy across targets, we can leave NATGW + conntrack bump as temporary and schedule permanent scaling and autoscale rules.

Nadia K: NLB target group health = 2/3 healthy at 2719994820; logs show successful TLS handshake now.

Tony R: Recommend we keep the conntrack increase only as temporary (non-persistent). We'll add a documented change to kernel params via a controlled rollout after a follow-up maintenance window and add alert to detect conntrack at >70% earlier.

Evan M: I'll add an alert to Sentry/Prometheus: conntrack_usage_percent > 60% for 5m -> page infra-owner. Also adding NAT port utilization alert > 80%.

Priya Patel: Customer update draft: "We've implemented temporary egress capacity and tuned connection tracking to restore external vendor connectivity. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a permanent scaling plan and root cause analysis. No change to packet source semantics was made." Approve?

Customer Support (Meridian): Approved. Please include estimated timeline for permanent fix.

Priya Patel: ETA for follow-up: 48 hours for autoscale rules & capacity commit. RCA doc will be published in 72 hours.

incident-bot: Incident status: Mitigated. Paging cleared. Severity downgraded to P2. Remember to run post-incident checklist and capture: timeline, mitigations, config diffs (conntrack sysctl, route table, NATGW id), and customer affected sessions count.

Alex Soto: NATGW id: nat-0a1b2c3d created. Route table meridian-private-rt now references nat-0a1b2c3d as secondary target. Will open change PR for persistent conntrack tuning after RCA.

Priya Patel: Thanks team. I'll start the RCA doc and ping Product/CS for customer communication. Please add any logs or bash snippets you used to the doc.

Evan M: Adding prometheus graphs and NLB access logs to the incident ticket.

Tony R: After-action items: (1) Implement connection pooling for outbound flows at proxy layer, (2) Harden alerts for conntrack + NAT port usage, (3) Validate autoscale headroom for each dedicated tenant pool. Assigning to Alex and Nadia.

Priya Patel: Closing the paging. If anything regresses, reopen the thread or page oncall. :white_check_mark:
